definitions.event: An accepted event record in the public corpus. Several records may share one filing.
definitions.filing: Unique SEC accession number in the common 90-day window.
definitions.recent: Latest recorded available_as_of in that window, not the date of the latest SEC filing in existence.
definitions.scope: Complete for the published corpus only. This is not comprehensive SEC coverage or independent verification.

notes.scope: Four selected public issuer documents. These dated notes are separate from the automated corpus counts and do not change them. Research interpretation is explicitly labelled.

notes.title: AWS growth: follow the operating economics.
notes.summary: AWS reported $17.773bn in operating income on $45.984bn in net sales. The segment grew 39.3% year over year.
notes.implication: Research implication: compare cloud operating profit with the capital required to deliver that growth.
notes.question: How much incremental cash investment supports AWS growth, and when does that capacity begin earning revenue?
notes.caution: The $184bn annualized revenue run rate is an extrapolation, not full-year realized revenue. Segment profit is not free cash flow.
notes.locator: Segment Information: AWS, three months ended September 30, 2026; Supplemental Financial Information: AWS margin.

notes.title: Two cash-flow numbers. A $2.240bn bridge.
notes.summary: Operating cash flow of $16.014bn less $4.011bn of capital expenditures gives $12.003bn. Adjustments add $2.240bn.
notes.implication: Research implication: separate operating cash generation from working-capital adjustments, asset proceeds and affiliate repayments.
notes.question: Which adjustments are repeatable enough to include in a forward cash model?
notes.caution: Both free-cash-flow measures are company-defined non-GAAP figures. Quarterly results are unaudited; adjusted cash flow is not interchangeable with the ordinary measure.
notes.locator: Attachment 3, Consolidated Statement of Cash Flows: Reconciliation of Non-GAAP Measures; Q3 2026 column.

notes.title: Future infrastructure costs need their own timeline.
notes.summary: Alphabet disclosed $130.5bn of future payments for leases that had not commenced, primarily for data centers and energy infrastructure.
notes.implication: Research implication: map future lease commencements separately from current lease liabilities and contingent backstops.
notes.question: When do these commitments become cash payments, and which obligations overlap across the notes?
notes.caution: These future payments were not yet recorded as lease liabilities. The separately disclosed $75.7bn of backstop support is contingent; adding the categories does not establish total debt.
notes.locator: Form 10-Q: Note 4, Leases; Liquidity and Capital Resources, Contingent Commitments.
notes.calculation: No aggregate debt total is computed from these categories.

notes.title: Separate cash generated from cash distributed.
notes.summary: ExxonMobil reported $9.4bn of shareholder distributions: $4.3bn in dividends and $5.1bn in repurchases.
notes.implication: Research implication: test whether operating cash generation can sustain investment and distributions across commodity-price scenarios.
notes.question: How sensitive is cash remaining after investment to prices, working capital and one-time items?
notes.caution: The release rounds these figures to billions. Free cash flow follows ExxonMobil’s definition. Announced 2027 repurchases are a future plan, not Q3 cash paid.
notes.locator: Exhibit 99.1: opening results summary, cash-flow and shareholder-distribution paragraphs.
